key_insight: Uni-HamGNN learns a universal, spin–orbit-coupled Hamiltonian from atomic structure, enabling fast, accurate prediction of electronic structure (including spin–orbit effects) across the periodic table for high-throughput materials discovery.
problem_solved: First-principles calculations that include spin–orbit coupling are accurate but computationally expensive and slow, limiting large-scale screening and discovery of quantum materials; there was no broadly transferable ML model that predicts spin–orbit-coupled electronic structure across diverse elements.
method: Graph neural network that encodes atomic/crystal graphs and outputs a spin–orbit-coupled Hamiltonian representation from structure.
Trained on ab initio electronic-structure data with physics-informed inductive biases so predictions generalize across many elements and material classes.
Efficient inference pipeline that converts predicted Hamiltonians into electronic properties (bands, gaps, topology) for rapid high-throughput screening.
impact: Provides AI/ML practitioners a transferable, physics-aware surrogate for costly electronic-structure calculations, enabling rapid screening, feature extraction, and downstream ML tasks for quantum/materials design.
visual_elements: Pipeline schematic: crystal structure -> GNN encoder -> predicted spin–orbit Hamiltonian -> band structure/PDOS
Parity plot: predicted vs. reference first-principles electronic energies or band gaps (accuracy and scatter)
Periodic-table heatmap showing model performance or predicted property trends across elements
Throughput/latency bar chart comparing runtime of Uni-HamGNN vs. traditional DFT with SOC
paper_title: A universal spin–orbit-coupled Hamiltonian model for accelerated quantum material discovery
paper_authors: Yang Zhong, Rui Wang, Xingao Gong, Hongjun Xiang
